newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge hostage urges end to fighting.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge hostage urges end to fighting.

text.p: A man purporting to be one of 15 government officials held by hardline Khmer Rouge guerrillas said on Monday that the missing group was safe.

Khmer Rouge radio broadcast a statement by a man identifying himself as negotiator General Nin Pin, one of 15 officials and pilots who flew into rebel held territory by helicopter on February 14 to negotiate the defection of guerrillas in northern Cambodia.
"We are are all right and we stay together. Our food is served normally and they give enough medicine to treat us, so there is no problem for us," Nin Pin said.
The government had demanded the officials be released soon and had been building up troops and armaments since the start of the month around the rebels' stronghold of Anlong Veng.

Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said last week he had received intelligence reports that only three hostages were alive. He blasted those behind the mission, which was organised by the royalist FUNCINPEC party of his rival, Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Nin Pin said Khmer Rouge officials had said late last week that negotiations would take time because they wanted to avoid the rivalry faced at bases such as Pailin, Phnom Malai and Samlaut, since the movement began to split last August.
"They said they need to check thoroughly to ensure the real national reconciliation," he said.
Ranariddh and Hun Sen have been competing for the loyalty of thousands of defectors in those northwest bases.
Tensions between rival Khmer Rouge in Samlaut, cradle of a peasant rebellion in 1967, triggered clashes and sent some guerrillas fleeing from the area.
Government and military officials in the north could not be reached for comment on the latest situation around Anlong Veng.

The Khmer Rouge, whose 1975-79 killing fields rule left more than one million people dead, reneged on a U.N.-brokered 1991 peace pact and have been fighting the coalition government formed two years later.
